find: # languette's shipped redactions: what a post to a public repo carries out of
# this machine without them. Pairs apply in file order on the running text,
# shipped then yours. $NAME is the hook's environment, quoted as a literal
# inside a re: find; $HOSTNAME alone is asked of the OS when unset, and a line
# naming a variable that is unset or empty is skipped. A path is
# not a longer path: ~2 and ~-backup are someone else's. /Users comes last: it
# is inside /mnt/c/Users and C:/Users, which go whole.

comment: the home directory as the shell spells it
the Windows spelling of it; a Windows account named unlike $USER is a line of your own
a name that resolves only on your network or tailnet; before $HOSTNAME so a full name goes whole
this machine's name, short or full; a hyphen or dot continues a name, so zephyr leaves zephyr-01 alone
RFC 1918, CGNAT (a tailnet) and link-local; a range such as 10.0.0.0/8 is left as written
